title: Formal smoothness for an adic topology passes to the completion
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $\mathfrak n\subseteq S$ a finitely generated ideal, $S^\wedge=\varprojlim_nS/\mathfrak n^n$ the $\mathfrak n$-adic completion of $S$ with $\iota:S\to S^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], an $R$-algebra via $\iota\circ\varphi$, and $\mathfrak nS^\wedge$ the ideal of $S^\wedge$ generated by $\iota(\mathfrak n)$. If $S$ is formally smooth over $R$ for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic], then $S^\wedge$ is formally smooth over $R$ for the $\mathfrak nS^\wedge$-adic topology.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07ED (lemma-formally-smooth-completion, line 9224), (1) implies (2), with R discrete (the zero ideal of R, finitely generated, R^ = R) and its proof (lines 9242-9251), which uses Algebra, Lemma Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated): S^/n^k S^ = S/n^k and n S^ = n^ for n finitely generated

proof.text: *Setup and the truncations of $S^\wedge$.* Write $\iota:S\to S^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]; $S^\wedge$ is an $R$-algebra via $\iota\circ\varphi$ and $\iota$ is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. For $m\ge1$ let $\pi_m:S^\wedge\to S/\mathfrak n^m$, $(x_j)_j\mapsto x_m$, and $p_m:S\to S/\mathfrak n^m$ the quotient map. Since $\mathfrak n$ is finitely generated, [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] (with $A=S$, $I=\mathfrak n$, $N=m$) gives: $\pi_m$ is a surjective homomorphism of $S$-algebras with $\pi_m\circ\iota=p_m$ and $\ker\pi_m=\mathfrak n^mS^\wedge$, the ideal generated by $\iota(\mathfrak n^m)$. As an $S$-algebra map it is an $R$-algebra map for the structures through $\varphi$: $\pi_m(\iota(\varphi(r)))=p_m(\varphi(r))$. This is the input 'the assumption that $\mathfrak n$ is finitely generated implies $S^\wedge/\mathfrak n^nS^\wedge=S/\mathfrak n^n$ (Algebra, Lemma 05GG)' of the source's proof.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07ED (lemma-formally-smooth-completion, line 9224), lines 9242-9251 (first sentence, citing Algebra, Lemma Tag 05GG, lemma-hathat-finitely-generated, algebra.tex line 22645)

proof.text: *$(\mathfrak nS^\wedge)^m=\mathfrak n^mS^\wedge=\ker\pi_m$ for $m\ge1$.* $(\mathfrak nS^\wedge)^m$ is generated by products $y_1\cdots y_m$ with $y_i\in\mathfrak nS^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]; writing each $y_i=\sum_l\iota(x_{il})s_{il}$ ($x_{il}\in\mathfrak n$, $s_{il}\in S^\wedge$) and expanding, $y_1\cdots y_m$ is a sum of terms $\iota(x_{1l_1}\cdots x_{ml_m})s$ with $x_{1l_1}\cdots x_{ml_m}\in\mathfrak n^m$, so it lies in $\mathfrak n^mS^\wedge$. Conversely $\mathfrak n^m$ is additively generated by products $x_1\cdots x_m$ ($x_i\in\mathfrak n$), and $\iota(x_1\cdots x_m)=\iota(x_1)\cdots\iota(x_m)\in(\mathfrak nS^\wedge)^m$, so $\iota(\mathfrak n^m)\subseteq(\mathfrak nS^\wedge)^m$ and $\mathfrak n^mS^\wedge\subseteq(\mathfrak nS^\wedge)^m$. With step 1, $\ker\pi_m=(\mathfrak nS^\wedge)^m$. (In the source: diagrams for $S$ with the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology and for $S^\wedge$ with the $\mathfrak n^\wedge=\mathfrak nS^\wedge$-adic topology have the same truncations.)

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07ED (lemma-formally-smooth-completion, line 9224), lines 9242-9251

proof.text: *The data of the lifting problem for $S^\wedge$, and the restricted problem for $S$.* By [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] (for $S^\wedge$ over $R$ and the ideal $\mathfrak nS^\wedge$) let $D$ be a commutative ring with a ring map $R\to D$, $J\subseteq D$ an ideal with $J^2=0$, $q:D\to D/J$ the quotient map [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and $g:S^\wedge\to D/J$ a homomorphism of $R$-algebras with $g((\mathfrak nS^\wedge)^k)=0$ for some $k\ge1$; we must find an $R$-algebra map $f:S^\wedge\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$. Put $g_0=g\circ\iota:S\to D/J$, a homomorphism of $R$-algebras (composite of two). For $x\in\mathfrak n^k$, $\iota(x)\in\iota(\mathfrak n^k)\subseteq(\mathfrak nS^\wedge)^k$ by step 2, so $g_0(\mathfrak n^k)=0$, with the same $k\ge1$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07ED (lemma-formally-smooth-completion, line 9224), lines 9242-9251 ('diagrams ... for the cases (1) and (2) are in 1-to-1 correspondence': a diagram for $S^\wedge$ restricts to one for $S$)

proof.text: *Lift over $S$.* $S$ is formally smooth over $R$ for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology, so by [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] applied to $D$, $J$, $q$ and $g_0$ (step 3) there is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $f_0:S\to D$ with $q\circ f_0=g_0$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07ED (lemma-formally-smooth-completion, line 9224), lines 9242-9251

proof.text: *$f_0$ kills $\mathfrak n^{2k}$* (remark (a) of [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic], written out). For $x\in\mathfrak n^k$, $q(f_0(x))=g_0(x)=0$, so $f_0(x)\in\ker q=J$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. The ideal $\mathfrak n^{2k}=\mathfrak n^k\mathfrak n^k$ is generated by products $xy$ with $x,y\in\mathfrak n^k$, and $f_0(xy)=f_0(x)f_0(y)\in J^2=0$; the set $\ker f_0$ is an ideal containing these generators, so $f_0(\mathfrak n^{2k})=0$. (Source, proof of Lemma 07EC (1), lines 9184-9197: '$\psi(\mathfrak n^k)\subset J$ hence $\psi(\mathfrak n^{2k})=0$ as $J^2=0$'.)

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07EC (lemma-formally-smooth, line 9165), part (1), lines 9184-9197, as used in the proof of Lemma 07ED

proof.text: *The lift over $S^\wedge$.* By step 5, $\ker p_{2k}=\mathfrak n^{2k}\subseteq\ker f_0$, so $f_0$ factors uniquely as $f_0=\bar f_0\circ p_{2k}$ with $\bar f_0:S/\mathfrak n^{2k}\to D$ a ring homomorphism (homomorphism theorem for the surjection $p_{2k}$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]); $\bar f_0$ is an $R$-algebra map because $f_0$ is and $p_{2k}$ is a surjective $R$-algebra map. Define $f=\bar f_0\circ\pi_{2k}:S^\wedge\to D$; by step 1 it is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras, and $f\circ\iota=\bar f_0\circ p_{2k}=f_0$. (This is the source's identification $S/\mathfrak n^{2k}=S^\wedge/\mathfrak n^{2k}S^\wedge$ used for the dotted arrows.)

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07ED (lemma-formally-smooth-completion, line 9224), lines 9242-9251

proof.text: *$q\circ f=g$.* By step 2, $\ker\pi_{2k}=(\mathfrak nS^\wedge)^{2k}\subseteq(\mathfrak nS^\wedge)^k\subseteq\ker g$, and $\pi_{2k}$ is surjective (step 1), so $g=\bar g\circ\pi_{2k}$ for a ring map $\bar g:S/\mathfrak n^{2k}\to D/J$. Then $\bar g\circ p_{2k}=\bar g\circ\pi_{2k}\circ\iota=g\circ\iota=g_0=q\circ f_0=q\circ\bar f_0\circ p_{2k}$, and $p_{2k}$ is surjective, so $\bar g=q\circ\bar f_0$. Hence $q\circ f=q\circ\bar f_0\circ\pi_{2k}=\bar g\circ\pi_{2k}=g$. So every lifting problem of [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] for $S^\wedge$ over $R$ with the ideal $\mathfrak nS^\wedge$ has a solution, i.e. $S^\wedge$ is formally smooth over $R$ for the $\mathfrak nS^\wedge$-adic topology.

split_report.summary: Statement checked against More on Algebra 07ED (more-algebra.tex line 9224), (1) => (2) with R discrete (m = 0): the DAG's def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic is 07NI with m = 0, and 07ED's n^ = nS^ is the ideal generated by iota(n) (05GG); statement kept. The source's proof (lines 9242-9251) says only that, by 05GG, diagrams for S and S^ are in 1-to-1 correspondence; written out in 7 steps exactly as the DAG's definition requires: (1) truncations pi_m: S^ -> S/n^m surjective R-algebra maps with pi_m o iota = p_m and kernel n^m S^ (existing Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power = 05GG); (2) (nS^)^m = n^m S^ (elementary); (3) restrict g to g_0 = g o iota, which kills n^k; (4) lift g_0 to f_0 by formal smoothness of S; (5) f_0 kills n^{2k} (J^2 = 0; remark (a) of the definition, 07EC(1)); (6) f = bar f_0 o pi_{2k}; (7) q o f = g, by factoring g through pi_{2k} (kernel (nS^)^{2k} inside (nS^)^k) and surjectivity of p_{2k}. Only 05GG (2)/'R^/I^nR^ = R/I^n' is used; completeness of S^ and n^ = (n)^ are not needed. No new node: 05GG is lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power (lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal and lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete are the n = 1 / module versions; lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-quotient is a different statement, 07PR). Citer lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-local-completion-formally-smooth checked: its step 5 uses exactly this statement with R = A, S = T, n = qT (finitely generated by its step 4). Mathlib: re-searched (LeanSearch, Loogle, LeanFinder, grep, local_search unavailable): no adic formal smoothness in Mathlib, so no match.
